questions.question: If 9 # 3 @ 2 = 10 and 11 # 4 @ 1 = 14, then 9 # 6 @ 9 = ?
questions.solution:
Logic: Here # means +, @ means -

9 # 3 @ 2 = 10

→ 9 + 3 - 2

→ 12 - 2 = 10

11 # 4 @ 1 = 14

→ 11 + 4 - 1

→ 15 - 1 = 14

Similarly,

9 # 6 @ 9

→ 9 + 6 - 9

→ 15 - 9

→ 6

Thus, ‘6’ is the correct answer.

You have to consider the statement and the following assumptions and decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement. Statement: The applicant was told that he was appointed as a programmer with a probation of one year and that his performance would be reviewed at the end of the period for confirmation. Assumptions: 1. The performance of an individual was generally not known at the time of appointment offer. 2. Generally an individual tries to prove his worth during the probation.
questions.questionHtml:
In the question  given below is given a statement followed by two assumptions numbered I and II. An assumption is something taken for granted. You have to consider the statement and the following assumptions and decide which of the assumptions is implicit in the statement.

Statement: The applicant was told that he was appointed as a programmer with a probation of one year and that his performance would be reviewed at the end of the period for confirmation.

 Assumptions:

1. The performance of an individual was generally not known at the time of appointment offer.

2. Generally an individual tries to prove his worth during the probation.

options.text: Neither assumption I nor II is implicit
options.html: Neither assumption I nor II is implicit

options.text: Both assumptions I and II are implicit
options.html: Both assumptions I and II are implicit

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Option 4".

Given:

Statement: The applicant was told that he was appointed as a programmer with a probation of one year and that his performance would be reviewed at the end of the period for confirmation.

Assumptions:

I. The performance of an individual was generally not known at the time of appointment offer - True (Because a probation period is provided to assess an employee's performance after appointment. This implies that the employer does not already have sufficient knowledge of the individual's actual job performance.)

II. Generally an individual tries to prove his worth during the probation - True (Because the purpose of a probation period is to evaluate an employee, and it is naturally assumed that the employee will make an effort to perform well in order to secure confirmation.)

So, both Assumptions I and II are implicit.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".

Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements. Statements: I. No tyre are white. II. All grey are white. Conclusions: I. No white is tyre. II. No tyre is grey. III. Some white are not grey.
questions.questionHtml:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

Statements:

I. No tyre are white.

II. All grey are white.

Conclusions:

I. No white is tyre.

II. No tyre is grey.

III. Some white are not grey.

options.text: Both conclusions I and III follows
options.html: Both conclusions I and III follows

options.text: Both conclusions I and II follows
options.html: Both conclusions I and II follows

questions.solution:
The pattern followed here is:

The least possible Venn diagram is shown below according to the given statements.

Statements:

I. No tyre are white.

II. All grey are white.

III. Some white are not grey.

Conclusions:

I. No white is tyre → Follow → As no tyre are white. So no white is tyre is definitely followed.

II. No tyre is grey → Follow → As no tyre are white and all grey are white. So no tyre is grey is definitely followed.

III. Some white are not grey → Does not follow → As all grey are white. So some white are not grey is not definitely followed.

So, Both conclusions I and II follow.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 3"

questions.question: A question is given followed by two arguments. Decide which of the arguments is/are strong with respect to the question. Question: Should the government encourage young entrepreneurs? Arguments: Ⅰ. Yes, they will reduce the burden of unemployment. Ⅱ. Yes, they will contribute to the development of the country.
questions.questionHtml:
A question is given followed by two arguments. Decide which of the arguments is/are strong with respect to the question.

Question:

Should the government encourage young entrepreneurs?

Arguments:

Ⅰ. Yes, they will reduce the burden of unemployment.

Ⅱ. Yes, they will contribute to the development of the country.

options.text: Both arguments Ⅰ and Ⅱ are strong.
options.html: Both arguments Ⅰ and Ⅱ are strong.

options.text: Neither argument Ⅰ nor Ⅱ is strong.

questions.solution:
From the given statement:

Should the government encourage young entrepreneurs? 

Now we consider the given arguments:

Ⅰ. Yes, they will reduce the burden of unemployment: Many entrepreneurs have innovative and great ideas but those ideas are not sufficiently implemented and if the government encourages young entrepreneurs, it will definitely reduce unemployment on large scale. Thus the argument is strong.

Ⅱ. Yes, they will contribute to the development of the country: With more and more interest in entrepreneurship from the young generation, it will be huge diversification of different fields and it will ultimately lead to the development of the country and this initiative from the government will inspire many young minds from an early age to think out of the box and come up with something different and new ideas. Therefore the argument is strong.

So, both arguments Ⅰ and Ⅱ are strong.

Hence the correct answer is option 1).

questions.question: A statement is given below, followed by four conclusions given in the options. Find out which conclusion is true based on the given statement. Statement: S < T ≤ G < M < K > P ≥ O
questions.questionHtml:
A statement is given below, followed by four conclusions given in the options. Find out which conclusion is true based on the given statement.

Statement: S < T ≤ G < M < K > P ≥ O
questions.solution:
Given Statement: S < T ≤ G < M < K > P ≥ O

Now,

Conclusions:

1. O = S = T → False (S < T ≤ G < M < K > P ≥ O It gives S < T ≥ O)

2. M ≥ P ≥ O → False (M < K > P ≥ O No relation can be established between M and P)

3. K > O > S → False (S < T ≤ G < M < K > P ≥ O it gives S < K ≥ O)

4. K > G > S → True (S < T ≤ G < M < K It gives K > G > S)

Here, Conclusions 4 follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
